newsitem.title: INDIA: India's TMC says up to Moopanar on joining govt.
newsitem.headline: India's TMC says up to Moopanar on joining govt.

text.p: Former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) on Sunday authorised its leader, G.K. Moopanar, to decide whether the regional party would join India's new government.

Party spokesman S. Gnanadesikan told reporters that the TMC executive committee welcomed the decision last week by TMC deputies in the federal parliament to recommend staying out of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's government.

"The executive committee unanimously decided to authorise party president G.K. Moopanar to take a decision taking into consideration national interest and the political future of the TMC in Tamil Nadu," Gnanadesikan told reporters in the southern city of Madras.
The TMC, part of the centre-left United Front coalition, decided on April 19 to stay out of the government after the alliance chose Gujral instead of Moopanar as its leader and next prime minister.

"The executive committee also welcomed the decision of the TMC parliamentary party to stay out of the government because its integrity had been questioned," Gnanadesikan said, referring to the view of TMC's 20 deputies in the federal parliament.
Party officials said TMC legislators in the Tamil Nadu assembly as well as district presidents pressed Moopanar at Sunday's meeting to keep the regional party out of Gujral's government.
They argued that joining Gujral's government would limit TMC's options in competing with the state's ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), also a part of the alliance.
